non_blocking_findings: Mutant survivor: replacing the SG_PREREQS pair planets-test:planet-assets with ship-console-test:import (a real target pair) keeps 4 pairs and 4 distinct, and script-gate-prereqs reports 4 pairs hold. The new pin SG_PREREQS_PAIRS counts pairs, not their names, so it kills a dropped pair but not a swapped one. Suggest pinning the sorted list text or a checksum of it.

Counted summaries are only required to be nonzero and to reject zero. Deleting a check from a test script, or a script that prints a hard-coded count, passes every gate; no per-gate count is pinned. Same as B3; by design in D1.

UNATTRIBUTED: the first AC5 run (rig load average about 9) failed ship-live-sim with 'FAIL normal startup (startup_timeout)' from tests/test_live_journey.gd; make ship-demo-live-test repeated it once, then passed on the third run (17 passed, 28 s), and the base test run directly passed in 56 s. The test and the sim startup are unchanged except the summary print, so I attribute it to a cold sim cache under load, not to the change. Worth knowing: the first run in a fresh clone can be red on a loaded rig.
The AC14 curl bound has no static gate: removing --max-time 60 survives script-gate-lint and every other gate, and is killed only by AC14 (a stalled server). AC14 is a manual AC, not in make test.

ship-demo-geometry-negative-test now has two gate lines for what was one baseline row (one per mutation). Correct, and the reason regexes are bound, but the 56-rows-to-57-lines mapping needs the explanation the doc gives in D2.

tools/ship_baseline.sh: --retry-max-time 120 does not cap an attempt that has started; the real bound is --max-time 60 per attempt (measured 121-123 s total for one file, 2 curl 28s). Fine, but multi-file fetches multiply it only on success paths.
